title: Cleopatra: Last Pharaoh's Final Act
description: Politics, romance, and myth around history’s most famous queen.

questions.question: Which queen, the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, was reportedly the first of her Greek dynasty to learn Egyptian?
questions.explanation: The Ptolemies descended from one of Alexander the Great's Macedonian generals. Mind-bender: she lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

questions.question: Which Roman leader did Cleopatra have a relationship with before Mark Antony?
questions.explanation: Plutarch says she reached him in 48 BC tied up in a bed-sack carried by her ally Apollodorus. The rolled-up carpet came later, courtesy of translators and Hollywood.

questions.question: What was the name of Cleopatra and Caesar's son?
questions.explanation: Plutarch says Alexandrians gave him that nickname: "little Caesar." After her death, Octavian had him killed, reportedly advised that too many Caesars was not a good thing.

questions.question: Having sent Caesarion away for safety, how does legend say Cleopatra died in 30 BC?
questions.explanation: Even Plutarch, our main source, admitted "the truth of the matter no one knows"; another rumor had poison hidden in a hollow comb. Octavian still paraded her image with the serpent.

questions.question: Cleopatra's legendary snake bite most likely came from which species—the same serpent that rears on pharaohs' crowns?
questions.explanation: Ancient writers said "asp"; historians who buy the story favor the cobra, whose venom kills quietly. Fitting: the rearing cobra, the uraeus, was Egypt's royal emblem. Others doubt any snake.

imageHint: The golden uraeus crown worn by ancient Egyptian rulers, symbol of pharaonic power
